description: Prompts for testing whether an asking or contract price is realistic against recent comparable sales — an indicative price check reported as a range (Over / Fair / Under), never a certified valuation and never with fabricated comps.

cards.title: Comparable Sales Price Check
cards.description: Bracket an asking or contract price against recent comparable sales and report whether it is Over, Fair, or Under the evidence — always as a range, never a single figure.
cards.prompt:
You are an Australian buyer-side price analyst. I want to know whether the price on this property is realistic before I negotiate or sign. This is an indicative price check, NOT a certified valuation — always report a range, and NEVER invent a comparable sale.

SUBJECT PROPERTY:
- Address: [full address, suburb, state, postcode]
- Type: [house / townhouse / unit / land]
- Attributes: [beds / baths / car spaces]
- Living area: [X m² — or 'unknown']
- Land area: [X m² — or 'unknown']
- Condition: [original / average / renovated / new — or 'unknown']
- Key features: [pool / views / main-road / flood-prone / none noted]

PRICE BEING TESTED: $[amount]
PRICE TYPE: [advertised asking / price guide / contract / auction expectation]

COMPARABLE SALES (paste 4–8 recent nearby sales — address, beds/baths/cars, land/living m², sale price, sale date, distance, source. If you don't have them, write 'none — please list where to get them'):
[paste here]

Please return exactly these 6 sections:
1. Subject & Price Being Tested
2. Comparable Sales Table (only real, sourced sales — never fabricate a row; if none are supplied or found, produce the data-source checklist and STOP)
3. Adjustments & Reasoning (floor/ceiling bracket + $/m² cross-check; flag market movement to verify, never assume growth)
4. Implied Value Range (low / most-likely / high — always a range)
5. Is the Asking Price Realistic? (OVER / FAIR / UNDER, by $ and %)
6. Confidence, Data Gaps & Questions for a Local Agent, Certified Valuer, and Broker

DISCLAIMER: General information and educational preparation only. This is an indicative price check, not a certified valuation — a mortgage, legal, tax (including CGT), or family-law purpose needs a Certified Practising Valuer (CPV / API). Not financial, credit, tax, legal, or investment advice. Verify every figure independently.
cards.best_for: Buyers who have an asking, price-guide, or contract figure and want to sanity-check it against real comparable sales before negotiating or signing
cards.output_type: 6-section price check including a sourced comparable-sales table, an implied value range, and an Over / Fair / Under verdict
cards.professional_review_note: This is an indicative price check, not a certified valuation. For any lending, purchase, sale, tax (including CGT), legal, or family-law purpose, obtain a formal valuation from a Certified Practising Valuer (CPV / API) or RICS registered valuer, and confirm any LVR shortfall risk with your mortgage broker.

cards.title: Comparable Sales Evidence Checklist
cards.description: Build the list of recent, close, similar sold properties needed for a defensible price check — before running the numbers — so no comparable is ever fabricated.
cards.prompt:
You are an Australian buyer-side research assistant. Before I test a price, I need to gather the right comparable sales so the price check is defensible. Never invent a sale, price, or date — only tell me how and where to find real ones.

SUBJECT PROPERTY:
- Address or suburb and state: [suburb, state, postcode]
- Type: [house / townhouse / unit / land]
- Attributes: [beds / baths / car spaces]
- Living / land area: [X m² / X m² — or 'unknown']
- Anything unusual: [pool / views / main-road / flood or fire overlay / heritage / none noted]

Please return:
1. What makes a strong comparable for THIS property (recency window, distance radius, matching type/attributes, condition, and features to match)
2. A source-by-source checklist of where to pull recent sold data (RP Data / CoreLogic, Domain Sold, realestate.com.au Sold, PropTrack / Pricefinder, State Valuer-General / Land Registry, local council) and what each is best for
3. How to label every figure with its source and date, and how to tell a confirmed sale price from a portal 'estimate' (never treat an estimate as a sale)
4. Red flags that make a comp misleading (superseded market, renovation between sale and listing, off-market or related-party sale, atypical land size)
5. A blank table format I can paste sales into, ready for a full price check

IMPORTANT: If genuine comparable sales can't be found, say so — do NOT fabricate comps to fill the gap.

DISCLAIMER: General information and educational preparation only. This supports an indicative price check, not a certified valuation. Not financial, credit, tax, legal, or investment advice. A valuation for any lending, legal, or tax purpose must come from a Certified Practising Valuer (CPV / API).
cards.best_for: Buyers and investors assembling the comparable-sales evidence for a property before running a price check, who want to make sure the comps are recent, close, similar, and real
cards.output_type: Comparable-selection criteria, a source-by-source data checklist, labelling and red-flag guidance, and a blank table ready for a price check
cards.professional_review_note: Comparable sales must be genuine and sourced — never fabricated. Confirm the closest recent sales with a local selling or buyer's agent, and obtain a formal valuation from a Certified Practising Valuer (CPV / API) for any lending, legal, or tax purpose.
